ticket: #17 pre 阶段 Semgrep 单文件临时根墙钟实测

env.dsh: 0.2.0-rc.1 (ticket assumed 0.2.1-rc.3; scan wall clock is independent of DSH)

ruleset.packing: single merged rules.yaml (one --config file); one-file-per-rule costs ~56 ms/file extra

protocol.measure: wall clock of: create unique temp root + write sample + empty .semgrepignore + spawn full `semgrep scan` + parse + delete root
protocol.cold: each iteration uses a fresh copy of rules.yaml under a new config dir (new disk bytes)
protocol.timeout: 45 s hard cap per run; 0 runs hit the cap in the final matrix

rule_count_curve.note: 2 KB sample.ts, warm, N=3, same host, earlier in the session

verdict.observed_min: 2769 ms (2 KB sample, warm, 1 of 5 runs)
verdict.cold_vs_warm: no material difference (+0.3% .. +1.6%); cost is dominated by CLI/core startup, not rule-file disk reads
verdict.size_effect: 2 KB vs 256 KB identical (~2.9 s) for TS; Python 256 KB adds ~4.2 s of rule matching
verdict.consequence: #13 D9 (synchronous pre-stage Semgrep with 1.2 s P50) is not achievable on this host with the stock CLI; #9 pre P50 <= 2 s is also unreachable. Pre path must change shape (persistent semgrep-core / batch / demote to post) or the budget must be redefined.

call_findings_for_13: --semgrepignore-filename does not exist; the flag is --x-semgrepignore-filename
an absolute Windows path for that flag fails with Fpath.add_seg: invalid segment (rc=2); pass a relative name with cwd at the temp root
--quiet makes osemgrep hand off to pysemgrep and is slower; do not pass it
one merged YAML is required: one config file per rule adds ~56 ms per file

stability.note: the full CLI intermittently wedges (0 CPU, >120 s) on this host; wedged runs were all excluded from the matrix above (final run: 40/40 rc=0)
known_cause_candidates: stdin/console handle inheritance on Windows (DEVNULL or piped parent stdio)
